claims.text: Rapid solidification of Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will induce a eutectic lamellar microstructure.
The induced microstructure will contain alternating soft BCC and hard B2-ordered phases.
A eutectic soft/hard lamellar architecture can provide a combination of high strength and high room-temperature ductility.
The phase balance produced in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will reduce density relative to the equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr baseline.
The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy is a random solid solution or coarse-grained single-phase BCC material.
The initial Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy has high density and typically low room-temperature ductility.
Post-solidification heat treatment can refine the lamellar spacing and stabilize B2 precipitates in the BCC matrix.
Cooling sufficiently rapidly can bypass equilibrium phase formation and produce a fine lamellar structure in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Heat treatment below the B2 solvus will prevent coarsening.
Fine regular lamellae store dislocations and thereby promote high strain hardening.
Hard B2 phases and nanoscale B2 precipitates pin dislocation motion.
An as-cast eutectic AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy exhibits a room-temperature σ_UTS/σ_0.2 ratio close to 16.
Dislocation storage and B2 pinning will prevent premature necking and improve ductility while retaining high strength in Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr.
Hf, Ti, and Zr permit phase-fraction tuning that lowers density relative to W/V-based RHEAs.
The processed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will have room-temperature yield strength greater than 1000 MPa.
The processed Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr alloy will have room-temperature tensile ductility greater than 10%.
Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr will have significantly lower density than NbMoTaWVTi because it contains neither W nor V.
Conventionally cast equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr has high strength but brittle room-temperature behavior.
The baseline brittleness arises from limited slip systems and high Peierls stress in the BCC structure.
Formation of TCP phases such as sigma or Laves phases would degrade ductility in RHEAs.

contradictions.description: The density comparator changes across fields. The main hypothesis claims a reduction relative to equiatomic Hf-Mo-Ta-Ti-Zr, whereas the predicted outcome and falsification rule compare density primarily with W/V-based RHEAs such as NbMoTaWVTi. Thus the experiment does not directly test the stated baseline-density claim.

The mediator specifies a BCC/B2 lamellar structure, but the microscopy measurement calls for confirming 'fcc/BCC and B2 phases,' introducing an FCC phase not present in the target structural hypothesis.

The prediction requires tensile ductility above 10%, but the falsification rule only treats ductility below 2% as failure. Results between 2% and 10% would violate the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis under the stated rule; yield strength below 1000 MPa is likewise omitted.
